:::info

La documentación de esta integración la escribe su autor y, por ahora, solo está disponible en inglés.

:::

Shows your **NRGkick Gen2** portable EV charger in Gladys through its **local
REST JSON API**: no cloud, no account, straight on your network.

> **Never tested with a real charger.** Not affiliated with DiniTech (the
> maker of the NRGkick). The integration talks to the charger as the
> nrgkick-api library (used by Home Assistant) does. DiniTech may change its
> API in an update.

## What you get

One device per charger, with:

| Feature                                    | Content                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Status                                     | No vehicle, plugged in not charging, charge paused, charging, waking, error |
| Connector                                  | Available, occupied, faulted or unavailable ("charging station" category)   |
| Charging state                             | Charging, vehicle connected, paused by the charger, idle                    |
| Vehicle plugged in, Charge paused          | Yes / no                                                                    |
| Power, and power L1 / L2 / L3              | In W                                                                        |
| Current L1 / L2 / L3, Voltage L1 / L2 / L3 | In A and V (a phase the attachment does not have stays empty)               |
| Charging current set                       | In A, the setpoint of the charger                                           |
| Current signaled to the vehicle            | In A                                                                        |
| Energy of the session                      | In kWh, a plain sensor (starts again at 0 at each session)                  |
| Energy index                               | In kWh, the total energy charged: an index, guarded (see below)             |
| Temperatures                               | Housing, attachment L1 / L2 / L3, in °C                                     |
| Error, warning, residual current device    | Yes / no, and the error and warning codes as text                           |
| Pause charging                             | Button, always available                                                    |
| Resume charging                            | Button (only when allowed)                                                  |
| Set the charging current                   | List from 6 A to the ceiling (only when allowed)                            |

Read every 30 seconds by default (10 s to 10 min, configurable).

## Installation

1. Give the charger a **fixed IP address** in your router.
2. In the **NRGkick app**, turn on the **local JSON API** (without it, the
   charger answers that the API must be turned on, and the status of the
   integration says so). If you also turn on **BasicAuth** there, note its
   user name and password.
3. Install the integration from the Gladys store. In its configuration,
   enter the **IP address of the charger**, and only when BasicAuth is on,
   its **user name** and **password** (both, or neither).
   A user name and a password pasted in the address (`admin:…@`) are
   ignored and never shown back: use the dedicated fields.
4. Save, then add the charger from the **Discovery** tab.

The password is **kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again**, and
sent only to the charger. It is never written to the logs, to `/data`, nor to
a state. The charger only speaks plain HTTP: the user name and the password
travel **in clear, over HTTP** on your local network. Keep the charger on a
trusted network.

The **Test the connection** button reads the charger once (at most every 10
seconds).

## Energy index

The total energy charged by the charger is an **index**: Gladys derives the
consumption and the cost from it, and counts every rise in full. The
integration guards it like the P1 Monitor integration does:

- never 0; a **drop** or an implausible **jump** (more than 25 kW on average
  since the last value; the charger delivers 22 at most) is **held**: the
  last accepted value is sent again, the status of the integration and the
  badge of the device show the kWh waiting, and the log says so; the hold is
  kept in `/data`, even across a restart;
- it is never confirmed by repetition nor by time: only the **"Accept the
  held index"** action of the configuration takes it, **in two clicks**. The
  first click takes nothing: it shows the value held (drop or jump, from →
  to, kWh). A second click within 60 seconds takes exactly that — the value
  shown, plus what the charger may have delivered since — and answers with
  what is counted; if the value changed meanwhile, it is shown again. Saving
  the configuration or a reconnection never accepts anything;
- a charger added again starts from a fresh guard.

The charger is usually behind your main meter: in the energy settings of
Gladys, put it under that meter so that it is not counted twice. The
**energy of the session** stays a plain sensor: it starts again at 0 at each
session, it is never an index.

## Commands

**"Pause charging"** is always available, without any option: it only stops
the charge (`charge_pause=1`). It is **never held back**: not by another
command in flight (it goes at once, and is sent once more when a resume it
overtook settles; a resume or a current not sent yet gives way), not by the
minute between two changes, not by a 429 pause or refused credentials (then
one request), not by a missing read (it needs none). When a resume was left
without confirmation, it may still reach the charger later: a pause sent
within the next 90 seconds is watched, and sent again (twice at most) if a
read shows the charge resumed while no other resume left from Gladys.
**Beware**: a resume made within these 90 seconds from the NRGkick app or
through OCPP is therefore cancelled too (twice at most); do it again after.

**A pause stays on the charger until a resume.** With the option below off
(the default), only the NRGkick app resumes the charge: a forgotten pause (by
a scene, the AI chat) may prevent the next charge and leave the car
uncharged. The charger may also refuse a pause (for instance when solar
charging blocks it): Gladys then answers "The charger refused the command".

Before the first read after a restart (a 429 pause or a block kept in
`/data`), the pause goes to the configured address for the last charger
read at that address only.

**"Resume charging"** and **"Set the charging current"** refuse every command
while **Allow resuming and the charging current** is off (the default). On:

- **Resume** sets `charge_pause=0` back; **refused without a vehicle plugged
  in**, or on an error or an unknown state;
- **Charging current**: from 6 A to the **ceiling**: the lowest of the
  "Ceiling of the charging current" of the configuration (16 A by default,
  32 A at most), the rated current of the charger and the max current of its
  attachment. If the charger takes another value than the one asked, Gladys
  shows "sent, without confirmation".
- **One change a minute at most** (resume or current): no fine regulation
  from Gladys.

They are **buttons** and a **list**, never switches: a "turn everything off"
(from Gladys, Google Home, Alexa or HomeKit) never reaches them. A scene can
trigger them, only through an explicit action. Note that the AI chat of
Gladys (MCP) can create and run such a scene: while the commands are
allowed, it can resume the charge or change the current.

Before a resume or a current change, the integration **reads the charger
again** and decides on that read only; the option is checked again right
before sending. A command without effect (already so) is not sent. A command
that cannot leave within 3.5 seconds is refused unsent. When the charger does
not confirm (silence, a 5xx error, an unexpected answer), Gladys shows
"Command sent, without confirmation": check the state, read again 5 then 20
seconds later. One command at a time: another one is refused at once, the
pause aside.

## Errors and limits

- **Charger unreachable**: only the connector ("unavailable") and the status
  ("Charger unreachable") change; the other values keep their last one. New
  try after 30 s, 1, 2, then 5 minutes, never faster than the interval.
- **JSON API turned off** in the app: the status says so; new try every 5
  minutes.
- **Credentials refused** (or asked for while none is entered): the status
  asks to check them. New tries after 15 minutes, 1 hour, then every 6
  hours, never sooner (kept in `/data` across a restart); saving new
  credentials tries again at once.
- **429 (too many requests)** or **5xx**: a pause (1 minute to 6 hours for a 429) for the reads and the commands but the pause of the charge, never
  shorter than the interval, kept in `/data` across a restart.
- Neither the energy limit nor the phase count are changed from Gladys in
  this version. One charger per integration. No Bluetooth.
- If your NRGkick also speaks OCPP to another software (for instance the
  OCPP integration of Gladys), both may contradict each other on the pause
  and the current: command only one of them.
- The logs never hold the text of the error answers of the charger, nor the
  password.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que NRGkick te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your NRGkick | `section` | No | Shows your NRGkick Gen2 portable charger in Gladys through its local REST JSON API, without any cloud: state, vehicle plugged in, power, current and voltage per phase, energy of the session, energy index, temperatures, codes. In the NRGkick app, turn on the local JSON API; give the charger a fixed address in your router. Enter its IP address, save, then add it from the Discovery tab. Pausing the charge is always possible from Gladys; resuming it and the charging current only if you allow them below. Never tested with a real charger. Not affiliated with DiniTech. |
| IP address of the charger | `string` | Sí | An IPv4 address or a host name, optionally followed by a port (80 by default). |
| User name (BasicAuth, optional) | `string` | No | Only if BasicAuth is on in the NRGkick app: its user name. Leave empty otherwise. |
| Password (BasicAuth, optional) | `secret` | No | Only if BasicAuth is on in the NRGkick app: its password. Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to the charger, in clear (HTTP) on the local network. Refused credentials are tried again after 15 min, 1 h, then every 6 h. |
| Allow resuming and the charging current | `boolean` | No | Off by default. On: Gladys may resume the charge (button) and set the charging current (list, 6 A to the ceiling below). Off: these two features refuse every command. "Pause charging" is always available: it only stops the charge, and the pause stays on the charger until a resume; with this option off, only the NRGkick app resumes it (a forgotten pause may prevent the next charge). |
| Ceiling of the charging current (A) | `number` | No | The highest current Gladys may ask for (16 A by default). The lower of this value, the rated current of the charger and the max current of its attachment applies. |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the charger is read, in seconds. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Used for the feature names of the devices added from now on, for the status texts and for the command errors. |

## Cómo instalar NRGkick en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: NRGkick aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-nrgkick:0.1.1`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-nrgkick](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-nrgkick).

NRGkick requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

NRGkick es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
